rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic nervous system reactivity causes systematic miscalibration of prediction intervals for high-reactivity individuals.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Subjects in the top 20% of sympathetic reactivity index will have coverage rates at least 15 percentage points lower than subjects in the bottom 80%, after controlling for per-subject classification accuracy.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for high-reactivity subjects is caused by the nonconformity score function (1 - predicted probability) having higher variance for extreme probability values, not by low feature density in the calibration set.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If nonconformity score variance drives undercoverage, coverage will correlate with the variance of predicted probabilities for high-reactivity subjects, and a variance-stabilized nonconformity score (e.g., logit-transformed) will eliminate the reactivity-coverage correlation.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Compute per-subject predicted probability variance during TSST; regress coverage on sympathetic reactivity index with and without probability variance as a covariate. Also test a logit-transformed nonconformity score (log(p/(1-p))) in Mondrian CP and compare reactivity-coverage correlation.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Reactivity-coverage correlation remains significant after controlling for probability variance, and logit-transformed nonconformity score does not eliminate the correlation.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Probability variance fully mediates the reactivity-coverage correlation, and logit-transformed nonconformity score restores nominal coverage for high-reactivity subjects.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Wrist-worn sensor (Empatica E4) motion artifacts during stress tasks disproportionately affect certain subjects, corrupting features used for nonconformity scoring.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: The interaction term (gesture_frequency × (6 - baseline_ACC_variance_proxy)) will significantly predict coverage rate (p < 0.05), with highest undercoverage in high-gesture/high-baseline-ACC-variance (loose-fit proxy) subgroup.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Undercoverage during TSST is caused by the model's inability to generalize to high-movement conditions, not by gesture-specific motion artifacts pooling in Mondrian bins.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If model generalization failure drives undercoverage, coverage will decline with overall movement intensity (ACC magnitude) for all subjects during TSST, regardless of gesture frequency or watch fit, and will not be specific to the predicted-stress bin.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Stratify by overall ACC magnitude (high/low) and predicted class. Test if coverage decline is specific to high-gesture/loose-fit subjects in predicted-stress bin (proposed) or occurs uniformly across high-movement subjects in both bins (rival).
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Coverage decline is specific to high-gesture/loose-fit subjects within the predicted-stress bin; low-movement subjects and non-stress bin show nominal coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Coverage declines with ACC magnitude across all subjects and both predicted classes, with no interaction between gesture frequency and watch fit.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Temporal non-stationarity in physiological stress trajectories violates the exchangeability assumption within Mondrian calibration folds for slow-responding subjects.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Slow recoverers (bottom 30% HRV recovery slope) will show a significant coverage decline from early to late calibration half (>10 percentage points), while fast recoverers will show no significant decline.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Coverage decline over calibration time is caused by sensor drift or battery depletion affecting all subjects equally, not by subject-specific recovery dynamics.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If sensor drift drives coverage decline, coverage will decrease over calibration time for both fast and slow recoverers with similar slopes, and the decline will correlate with sensor-level metrics (e.g., battery voltage, temperature) rather than HRV recovery.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Fit mixed-effects model: coverage ~ recovery_phenotype * calibration_time_half + sensor_drift_metric + (1|subject). Test if recovery_phenotype × time interaction remains significant after controlling for sensor drift metrics.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Recovery phenotype × time interaction is significant (p < 0.05) after controlling for sensor drift; slow recoverers show steeper coverage decline in late calibration half.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Sensor drift metric explains the time effect; recovery phenotype × time interaction becomes non-significant when sensor drift is included.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Mondrian taxonomy based on predicted class alone ignores continuous stress intensity, causing undercoverage for subjects at extreme intensity levels within each class.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Coverage rate will decrease monotonically with predicted probability within the predicted-stress bin; coverage for severe stress (prob >0.9) will be at least 15 percentage points lower than for mild stress (prob 0.5-0.7).
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: The coverage gap at extreme intensities is caused by the nonconformity score function (1-p) having higher variance for extreme probabilities, not by the binary taxonomy pooling.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If nonconformity score variance drives the gap, a variance-stabilized nonconformity score (e.g., logit-transformed) will eliminate the coverage gap across predicted probability deciles within the predicted-stress bin, even with the same binary taxonomy.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Apply logit-transformed nonconformity score (log(p/(1-p))) in Mondrian CP with binary taxonomy; compute coverage per predicted probability decile. Compare coverage gap between mild (0.5-0.7) and severe (>0.9) stress before and after transformation.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Coverage gap persists (>10pp) with logit-transformed nonconformity score under binary taxonomy.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Coverage gap closes (<5pp) with logit-transformed nonconformity score under the same binary taxonomy.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Subject-specific sensor-skin interface impedance (especially for EDA) creates systematic feature distribution shifts that violate the identical distribution assumption within taxonomy bins.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Coverage rate will show a significant quadratic relationship with EDA tonic level (U-shaped), with lowest coverage for tonic <0.5µS and >15µS, after controlling for HR max, HRV, and respiration rate.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Coverage variation with EDA tonic level is mediated by the model's feature weighting (e.g., over-reliance on EDA features for extreme tonic values), not by sensor-skin impedance artifacts.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If model feature weighting drives the U-shape, retraining the model with EDA features down-weighted or removed will eliminate the quadratic coverage-tonic relationship, while impedance artifacts would persist regardless of model architecture.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Train two models: (1) full feature set, (2) EDA features removed or down-weighted. Run Mondrian CP with both; test quadratic tonic-coverage relationship for each. If U-shape disappears with EDA removal, rival wins.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: U-shaped coverage-tonic relationship persists even when EDA features are removed or down-weighted in the model.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: U-shaped relationship disappears when EDA features are removed or down-weighted, indicating model weighting mediates the effect.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: The nonconformity score function (e.g., 1 - predicted probability) is poorly calibrated for subjects with atypical feature covariance structure, causing systematic undercoverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Coverage for high-Mahalanobis subjects (top 5%) will be <80% with class-conditional Mondrian, but will restore to ≥85% with k-NN Mondrian (k=10) using same model probabilities.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Miscalibration for atypical subjects stems from the nonconformity score (1-p) being insensitive to feature-space density, not from the class-conditional taxonomy failing to correct feature-conditional miscalibration.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If nonconformity score insensitivity drives miscalibration, a density-aware nonconformity score (e.g., 1-p weighted by local feature density) will restore coverage for high-Mahalanobis subjects even with class-conditional taxonomy.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Compare three approaches on high-Mahalanobis subjects: (1) class-conditional Mondrian with 1-p, (2) k-NN Mondrian with 1-p, (3) class-conditional Mondrian with density-weighted nonconformity score. Test which restores coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: k-NN Mondrian (2) restores coverage to ≥85% while density-weighted class-conditional (3) does not.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Density-weighted class-conditional (3) restores coverage to ≥85% while k-NN Mondrian (2) does not.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Finite calibration set size combined with rare subject phenotypes leads to high variance in empirical quantile estimates for those subjects' effective taxonomy bins.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Coverage for phenotypes with n_bin < 10 will be significantly below 1-α (90%), with deficit inversely proportional to √n_bin. Simulated coverage will converge to 90% as n_bin increases via synthetic augmentation.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Undercoverage for rare phenotypes is caused by the nonconformity score distribution having heavier tails for these phenotypes, not by finite-sample quantile estimation variance.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: If heavy tails drive undercoverage, the empirical quantile bias will not decrease with increasing n_bin (simulated), and a robust quantile estimator (e.g., trimmed mean of order statistics) will restore coverage without increasing n_bin.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Simulate coverage vs n_bin by bootstrapping calibration samples for rare phenotypes. Fit coverage = 1-α - c/√n_bin. Also test a robust quantile estimator (e.g., 0.95 quantile of nonconformity scores) at original n_bin.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Simulated coverage converges to 90% as n_bin increases (c > 0 significant); robust quantile estimator at original n_bin does not fully restore coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Simulated coverage plateaus below 90% even at large n_bin (c not significant); robust quantile estimator restores coverage at original n_bin.
